component.name: OpenStream100
component.summary: Control PipeWire applications with Hercules Stream 100 hardware

description.p: OpenStream100 provides up to eight pages of four per-application PipeWire volume and mute controls for Hercules Stream 100 hardware on Fedora Linux. Its desktop control panel manages channel assignments, custom channel colours and mixer backgrounds, custom button-label overlays, selectable mono or stereo activity meters with four visualiser styles, knob sensitivity, programmable buttons and LEDs, full-screen image and notepad content, a resizable mouse-controlled virtual mixer, a PIN-paired Android remote with per-device revocation, sign-in startup, service status, and the controller's full-screen 480x272 display.
Adds the Android remote mixer with mDNS discovery, GUI-approved PIN pairing, QR fallback, persistent device credentials, smooth faders, and application icons.
Adds configurable Notepad typography, an aspect-locked hardware-styled virtual mixer, shared crisp channel icons, and page-safe hardware icon caching.
Matches the firmware-owned lower separators to the Notepad card while preserving image and mixer compositor settings.
Adds a saved full-screen Notepad mode for typed or pasted reference notes while keeping all hardware controls active.
Preserves independent stereo rendering in the native Segmented visualiser by applying its required E053 companion mode.
Adds the Stream 100 firmware's four full-height native visualiser styles while preserving live stereo activity, volume markers, and percentage badges.
Restores the full-height Classic meters and their separate percentage badges, and removes rejected experimental styles from the settings UI.
Removes unsafe continuous framebuffer animation and combines distinctive custom decoration with the proven native live stereo and volume objects.
Attempts committed indexed-plane animation for custom visualisers, removed in 0.15.5 after hardware feedback.
Adds genuinely distinct Segmented, Rounded, and Slim visualiser silhouettes.
Adds the saved four-style visualiser selector and its initial native mapping, corrected in 0.15.3.
Adds a saved Mono or Stereo activity-monitoring selector to the control panel.
Adds independent left and right PipeWire activity capture and native stereo visualisers.
Adds validated custom button-label overlay imports and an exportable 480x80 PNG design template.
Adds a saved live hardware screen-brightness slider without display redraws.
Uses PipeWire-Pulse per-stream monitors to deliver reliable application activity peaks.
Keeps the paired activity meters continuously refreshed while preserving independent white volume markers.
Separates the white volume marker from paired coloured live-activity meters.
Keeps live visualizer streams attached across paused application states and reports decoded activity levels.
Targets application monitor streams by WirePlumber node name and reports visualizer connection failures.
Adds true audio-reactive native meters with a selectable current-volume fallback.
Uses the supplied native-resolution transparent OpenStream100 artwork for the persistent branded display.
Adds a persistent display broker so mixer restarts retain the clean resident logo and skip cold USB display initialization.
Neutralizes the late captured native layout that reactivated faders and action-zone lines over the startup logo.
Uses the controller's official complete reset batch to remove inherited native surfaces before the startup logo is composed.
Allows the mixer to complete and cache its graceful logo transition before systemd stops the display helper.
Leaves the OpenStream100 logo resident during graceful stops so the following startup can begin with matching logo content.
Uses the last resident LCD image for the unavoidable visible first composition, then transitions cleanly to the logo and Mixer.
Moves the startup brightness gate ahead of the first captured display-layout command.
Resets all eight inherited native-meter surfaces during initialization and gates the backlight earlier.
Clears captured native-panel activations inside initialization to prevent the inherited mixer from flashing during startup.
Preserves and correctly composites transparency in startup, background, and full-screen artwork.
Repeats native surface cleanup during first-frame composition and applies a darker startup-artwork response curve.
Suppresses captured startup surfaces and presents the supplied logo at a panel-safe brightness.
Uses the supplied OpenStream100 startup artwork and shortens the hidden primer sequence.
Blends compact badge margins with the active background and reduces application-label size.
Fixes striped compact badges by using stable opaque panel-coloured margins.
Reduces the visible percentage badges to give application labels and native meters more space.
Restores the controller's original paired meters below application names using compact native updates.
Moves volume bars into the proven percentage-badge objects so they remain visible in the full-screen mixer layout.
Adds configurable native volume bars and removes the redundant volume caption from each mixer column.
Replaces page-specific colour palettes while the display remains visible, eliminating the deliberate black page-transition interval.
Keeps custom-background palettes stable so ordinary mixer-page changes redraw without a black interval.
Redraws static application labels and safely replaces colour palettes when changing mixer pages.
Adds up to eight mixer pages with four channels and programmable actions per page, plus next-page and previous-page navigation.
Corrects the remaining swapped physical inputs for programmable Buttons 2 and 3.
Corrects the physical input order of all four programmable buttons while preserving native LED illumination.
Ensures portable test installations use their updated mixer service when an older RPM is already installed.
Adds assignable microphone, speaker, media and preset channel-volume actions for all four programmable buttons, with native LED illumination.
Adds a saved 0.5% to 4.0% knob-sensitivity control while preserving the original 1.0% response by default.
Restores zero-brightness initialization after hardware testing the one-percent experiment.
Starts native compositor warm-up at one-percent brightness directly from the initialization batch.
Uses a fully black primer palette to mask stale firmware layers during first-frame convergence.
Uses an active black primer before revealing the branded startup framebuffer.
Latches minimum startup brightness before the hidden active-panel redraw begins.
Primes the initial compositor through a minimum-brightness redraw before revealing the loading screen.
Extends dark first-frame settling so only the completed loading screen is illuminated.
Allows the first generated framebuffer to settle before revealing the branded startup screen.
Hides the non-atomic transition from the startup framebuffer into the saved screen.
Hides captured initialization layers until the complete OpenStream100 startup frame is ready.
Adds a branded startup display and a palette-safe transition into the saved screen mode.
Introduces the OpenStream100 name and displays the application version in the control panel.
Removes the remaining firmware dividers from full-screen image mode.
Removes the remaining firmware dividers from full-screen image mode.
Adds a separate edge-to-edge image mode while retaining live audio controls.
Adds custom background images while retaining compact, tear-free live updates.
Corrects hardware palette selection and native badge colour ordering.
Adds saved custom colours to all four mixer channels.
Initial Fedora RPM release with the hardware-validated v48 mixer.
